🇺🇸 INSIGHT : The CLARITY Act isn’t dead after failing a key Senate vote 49-50, with Sen. Thom Tillis’ motion to reconsider leaving the door open for another vote this session. Seven Democrats who voted against advancing the bill say they remain committed to crypto market structure legislation. But with ethics provisions still a major sticking point and the Senate heading into recess Oct. 2, the window for a 2026 deal is narrowing. News | Markets | YouTube

Financial Data and Ratings Giant S&P Global to Acquire Smart Contract Security Firm OpenZeppelin S&P Global has entered into an agreement to acquire OpenZeppelin, a leading smart contract security company, as it expands its digital asset risk assessment capabilities into onchain technology. Founded in 2015, OpenZeppelin develops one of the industry's most widely used open-source smart contract libraries and has completed more than 900 security engagements. Following the acquisition, OpenZeppelin will continue to operate under its own name as a separate business unit, led by CEO Demian Brener. Financial terms were not disclosed. — link

Just In: SEC Approves Innovation Exemption for Tokenized U.S. Stocks to Trade via Onchain AMMs The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) announced that it has officially approved a temporary, conditional exemptive framework (the "Innovation Exemption") to allow limited pilot trading of tokenized National Market System (NMS) stocks on specific onchain platforms known as Tokenized Securities Venues (TSVs). The exemption provides temporary regulatory relief to TSVs, ensuring they are not immediately classified as "exchanges" under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 when offering tokenized equities through permissioned automated market makers (AMMs) and liquidity pools, while also establishing clear guidelines for liquidity providers deploying proprietary capital for market-making support. The SEC’s Innovation Exemption sets four key conditions for Tokenized Securities Venues (TSVs): 1. Sanctions compliance: A TSV must be a U.S. person and comply with economic and trade sanctions administered and enforced by the U.S. Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC). 2. Permissioned access: A TSV must establish access standards and allow only eligible participants to trade tokenized NMS stocks on the venue. 3. No synthetic stocks: TSVs may only trade tokenized NMS stocks issued by or on behalf of the underlying issuer, or tokenized by an unaffiliated third party. The tokenized stock must provide holders with the same rights and privileges as the traditional security, including dividend and voting rights. 4. Issuer opt-out: Issuers must be given the opportunity to object to and prevent their securities from trading on a TSV. — link

CFTC Extends Phantom No-Action Relief to Eligible Passive Software Providers The U.S. CFTC’s Market Participants Division (MPD) issued Staff Letter 26-25, extending the no-action position previously granted to Phantom to eligible passive software providers, including those outside the crypto sector. Subject to specified conditions, such software may serve as a front-end interface enabling users to access registered futures commission merchants, introducing brokers, and designated contract markets, and submit orders directly for CFTC-regulated derivatives, including event contracts and perpetual contracts. The software may not custody user assets, generate explicit buy or sell signals, or exercise discretion over order routing or execution. — link
